# Summary of 2001 UK Political Manifesto

This manifesto outlines policies across multiple areas with the stated themes of freedom, justice, and honesty.

## Health
The manifesto proposes cutting NHS waiting times by recruiting 27,500 additional nurses, 4,600 doctors, and 10,250 allied health professionals. It includes providing 10,000 extra hospital beds and increasing pay for lower-paid NHS staff by £1,000 annually. The policy would end charges for dental and eye checks and have the state cover long-term personal care costs. The manifesto criticises centralised NHS management and proposes giving medical professionals greater autonomy.

## Education
Key proposals include reducing average class sizes to 25 pupils for ages 5-11, recruiting 5,000 extra secondary teachers, and increasing funding for books and equipment. University tuition fees would be abolished throughout the UK, with restored grants for poorer students. The National Curriculum would be replaced with a less rigid "Minimum Curriculum Entitlement." These measures would be funded through a one penny increase on income tax.

## Law and Order
The manifesto proposes recruiting 6,000 extra police officers and 2,000 part-time community officers. It emphasises crime prevention over prison expansion, focusing on rehabilitation programmes and reducing reoffending. Victims would gain greater rights to be heard in court. The policy opposes mandatory sentencing and would retain jury trials.

## Transport
Proposals include free off-peak bus travel for pensioners and disabled people, half-price travel for under-19s in education, and abolishing car tax for less-polluting vehicles. The manifesto criticises rail privatisation and proposes establishing stronger public control over railways through a Sustainable Transport Authority.

## Pensions and Benefits
The manifesto proposes increasing basic state pension by £5 weekly for single pensioners, with larger increases for over-75s and over-80s. This would be funded by a new 50% tax rate on incomes exceeding £100,000. It supports annual review of the minimum wage and extending it equally to all workers aged 16 and over.

## Constitutional Reform
Proposals include reforming voting systems using the AV+ system recommended by the Jenkins Commission, replacing the House of Lords with an elected Senate, and strengthening devolution. Local authorities would gain more powers, and council tax would be replaced with local income tax.

## Environment
Environmental policies run throughout the manifesto, including targets for 10% renewable energy by 2010, phasing out nuclear power, household recycling programmes, and reducing CO2 emissions. The manifesto opposes commercial GM crop growing pending safety research.

## European Union
The manifesto supports EU membership while advocating reform, including establishing an EU constitution defining and limiting powers, making the Commission more accountable, and supporting enlargement to include Central and Eastern European nations. It supports potential euro membership subject to referendum.

## Economy
Fiscal proposals include increased income tax for education funding, a 50% top tax rate on earnings over £100,000, and closing capital gains tax loopholes. The manifesto supports Bank of England independence and eventual euro membership at a competitive exchange rate.
